candidate.title: Prepare resume answers for job forms

demandEvidence.chore: Enter resume information into forms tailored to each company’s hiring process.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet that maps supplied resume facts to draft answers for repeated job-application fields.
inputs: Fictional resume facts supplied by the tester
A small set of manually transcribed sample form field labels
experimentPlan.trigger: When a tester receives another application form with fields represented in the sample set.
steps: Enter fictional resume facts into a structured table.
Add the sample form field labels.
Suggest matching facts for each field.
Flag fields with no clear match instead of guessing.
Have a person review and copy approved answers manually.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each sample field, verify the suggested answer matches the corresponding fictional resume fact and leaves uncertain fields blank.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must provide lawful test inputs, check every answer, handle sensitive information safely, and complete the actual application.
unverified: Actual employer form layouts and field variations are unavailable.
No supplied source supports form reading, browser automation, or automatic submission.
Whether job seekers or career services would pay is unknown.

ease.reason: A student can test extraction into a review table, but the source gives no form fields or supported software reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers or career services might value reducing repeated form entry; this post establishes no payment intent.

feasibility.reason: A draft-only test with fictional resume facts and sample fields is bounded; real employer forms and validation are unavailable.

autonomy.reason: A tool could suggest field values, but a person must verify every answer and submit each application; submission is unsupported.

evidence.reason: The post states repeated resume-data entry into company-specific forms, but gives no form examples, frequency beyond this account, or corroboration.

candidate.reason: The concrete repeated data-entry chore supports a proposed draft-only test, but there is no field-level or implementation evidence and the provisional mean is below six.

source.title: Tech market feels like a data entry job
source.text: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.
